jobs.name: clickup-executor
jobs.prompt:
Follow the clickup-queue-poller skill's claim step to claim exactly one ready ClickUp task (fenced executor lock applies — if another fenced executor owner is active, exit cleanly, claim nothing). Do NOT work the task in this session.

Instead hand it to a kanban swarm:
  hermes kanban swarm "<task goal>" --worker coder:"implement" --verifier ops --synthesizer coder --idempotency-key <clickup-task-id> --json

Capture `synthesizer_id` from that JSON. Poll `hermes kanban show <synthesizer_id> --json` every ~30s, reading `.task.status`:
  - "done" -> take the deliverable from `.task.result`, post it to the ClickUp task as a comment, move the task to In Review (never Complete — ignite-validate owns Complete).
  - "blocked" -> stop polling; post a ClickUp comment reporting the blockage (include `.latest_summary` / the blocking run's error) and leave the task for a human/next tick — do not loop forever.
  - anything else -> keep polling.
Cap total polling at 30 minutes; if still not done/blocked by then, post a timeout comment to ClickUp and exit — never hang the tick. If claim finds nothing ready, exit cleanly with no swarm spawned.

jobs.name: content-lane-executor
jobs.prompt:
Follow the clickup-queue-poller skill's content-lane claim rules to claim exactly one ready content-lane ClickUp task (fenced executor lock applies). Do NOT draft the piece in this session.

Instead hand it to a kanban swarm:
  hermes kanban swarm "<task goal>" --worker content:"draft" --verifier ops --synthesizer content --idempotency-key <clickup-task-id> --json

Capture `synthesizer_id` from that JSON. Poll `hermes kanban show <synthesizer_id> --json` every ~30s, reading `.task.status`:
  - "done" -> take the deliverable from `.task.result`, post it to ClickUp as a comment, move the task to In Review (never Complete).
  - "blocked" -> stop polling; post a ClickUp comment reporting the blockage (include `.latest_summary` / the blocking run's error) and leave the task for a human/next tick — do not loop forever.
  - anything else -> keep polling.
Cap total polling at 30 minutes; if still not done/blocked by then, post a timeout comment to ClickUp and exit.

Sonnet-only hard rule: the content profile ships with no fallback provider. If a swarm worker run fails closed because claude-sonnet-5 is unavailable, report that failure verbatim in the ClickUp comment — never retry on a different model yourself.

Folded from research-stage-monitor: as part of this tick also run `python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/research-stage-monitor-cron.py` and, if it reports anything other than healthy / disabled-or-smoke-only, include a one-line note of its status (post it as a ClickUp comment on the claimed task if one was claimed this tick, otherwise just note it in your own run output — do not open a new ClickUp task for it).

jobs.name: clickup-lifecycle
jobs.prompt:
Fold of clickup-closeout-audit + clickup-stalled-reconciler + clickup-reconciler + staleness-sweep into one ClickUp hygiene pass, every 30 minutes. Run each existing check via Bash, IN ORDER, and report/act on its own output — do not reinvent their logic, just orchestrate and surface what each one finds:

1. `python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/clickup_closeout_audit.py` — audits tasks that should have moved to Complete/closed and didn't (was daily 0 8 * * *, now runs every tick).
2. `python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/stalled_task_reconciler.py` — reconciles tasks stuck In Progress/In Review past their SLA.
3. `python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/staleness_sweep.py` — sweeps for generally stale/no-touch tasks (was offset 30 */6 * * *, now runs every tick).
4. Reconcile ClickUp drift (replaces the disabled clickup-reconciler agent job): follow the clickup-queue-poller skill's reconcile mode against any drift the three checks above surface — e.g. a kanban swarm marked done whose ClickUp task never moved to In Review.

Run each step to completion before starting the next. If any step exits nonzero, include its stderr verbatim in your summary — never suppress a failure to make the pass look clean. Never mark a ClickUp task Complete yourself; In Review only.

jobs.name: fleet-health-digest
jobs.prompt:
Fold of hermes-self-report + hermes-self-report-delivery-probe + skill-size-monitor + ignite-model-deprecation-check + supabase-rls-guard + hermes-usage-alert into one status pass every 6 hours.

Step 1 — build the digest exactly as hermes-self-report always has: read ${HERMES}/skills/hermes-self-report/SKILL.md (or use the attached skill content) and follow it: fan out to parallel delegated subagents for mechanical health / ClickUp activity (trailing 6h) / stuck signals, then compose the plain-text digest.

Step 2 — before sending, also run each of these via Bash and fold any non-clean result into its own digest section (never suppress a failure just to keep the digest looking clean):
  - `python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/hermes_self_report_delivery_probe.py` (prior delivery health)
  - `python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/hermes_validate_size_monitor.py` (skill-size guard)
  - `bash /Users/colingreig/dev/ignite-skills/ignite-model-deprecation-check.sh` (provider catalog deprecation check)
  - `python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/supabase_rls_guard.py` (Supabase RLS drift)
  - `python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/hermes_usage_alert.py` (provider/credential exhaustion + stuck-cron alarms — this script already posts its own Slack alert on trip; do not duplicate that post, just note in the digest whether it fired)

Step 3 — send the composed digest via postmark_send_report.py to colin@colingreig.com — pre-authorized, do not ask for confirmation, this is the one standing exception.

This is a READ-ONLY reporting tick: do not edit any cron/config/skill/ClickUp state no matter what you find; report it in the email instead. Complete in this single tick — do not ask the operator for permission to send.

jobs.name: repo-maintenance
jobs.prompt:
Fold of repo-worktree-gc + cleanup-hermes-baks + orphan-unpushed-monitor into one daily repo-hygiene pass at 04:00. Run each via Bash, IN ORDER, and report failures verbatim rather than suppressing them:

1. `python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/repo_gc_sweep.py` — garbage-collects stale git worktrees.
2. `python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/cleanup_hermes_baks.py` — prunes old `.bak-*` snapshot files.
3. `bash ~/.hermes/scripts/orphan_unpushed_cron.sh` (from /Users/colingreig/dev/hermes-agent) — flags orphaned unpushed branches/commits.

This is destructive-adjacent housekeeping (deletes worktrees and .bak files). If any script's own dry-run/safety gate blocks an action, respect the block and report it — never force past a script's own safety check.
